scope_note: Primary papers and official author-publication records only. Search-index body excerpts remain stored_search_excerpt. Opened primary abstract uses publisher_abstract; opened body passage uses reference_section. No external LLM API. General mechanism cards only; no actionable pathogen or toxin engineering.

evidence.retrieved_excerpt: These polycationic blockers traverse a long (>70 Å) pore, displacing multiple permeant ions
evidence.limits: Primary pore-scanning chemistry and electrophysiology distinguish a blocker migration barrier from binding affinity. Do not claim polyamines account for every component of inward rectification.

evidence.retrieved_excerpt: cytoplasmic domain that occludes the ion-conducting pore
evidence.limits: Primary 1990 peptide rescue of deletion mutant; free peptide action is concentration dependent and not noticeably voltage dependent. Tethered open-state access, rather than just blocker identity, is the boundary with mobile polyamines.

evidence.retrieved_excerpt: A four-step cycle driven by PI(4)P hydrolysis
evidence.limits: Primary reconstitution: OSBP tethering and lipid exchange, followed by ER Sac1 hydrolysis of returned PI4P, creates directional sterol transport. Other exchanged lipid identities are not additional cards.

evidence.retrieved_excerpt: outward-open to outward-occluded entails a prominent local rearrangement
evidence.limits: Opened Nature author abstract. GLUT3 outward-open/occluded structures are compared with GLUT1 inward-open, so the full dynamic cycle was inferred from related static structures, not filmed. Passive-carrier card does not claim pumping.

evidence.retrieved_excerpt: filaments grow at one end and shorten simultaneously at the other
evidence.limits: Primary radiolabeled subunit incorporation/release; abstract explicitly connects sustained treadmilling with irreversible ATP dephosphorylation. Not the mere head-to-tail orientation of actin subunits.

evidence.retrieved_excerpt: decarboxylation occurs directly upon reduction of the excited flavin by the fatty acid substrate
evidence.limits: Primary time-resolved spectroscopy/crystallography and computations. Card omits disputed exact bicarbonate-production route. Photoinitiated electron transfer and radical return distinguish the path from thermal protodecarboxylation.

evidence.retrieved_excerpt: In Crystallo Capture of a Covalent Intermediate
evidence.limits: Primary H63A UGM mutant crystal captures the flavin N5-sugar C1 covalent intermediate. Reduced flavin acts nucleophilically despite no net oxidation-state change; mutation-trapped structure does not directly observe every wild-type turnover step.

supplementary.note: Primary 2009 reduced substrate complex poised for covalent flavin catalysis.

evidence.retrieved_excerpt: direct evidence for the Fl(N5[O]) species via isotope labeling, proteolytic digestion, and high-resolution tandem mass spectrometry
evidence.limits: Opened PubMed author abstract and figure captions. N5 oxide is established; radical coupling and water loss in regeneration remain proposed. Downstream Favorskii rearrangement is excluded from this card.

supplementary.note: 2013 primary oxygenation-dehydrogenation report originally proposed N5 oxide; 2015 source directly tests it.

evidence.retrieved_excerpt: formation of dead-end prenylated flavin mononucleotide cycloadducts occurs with distinct propenoic and propiolic acids
evidence.limits: Opened Nature Chemistry primary author abstract. Atomic-resolution analog adducts, enzyme mutation and calculations support reversible cycloadduct route and strain dependence. Not every UbiD substrate has the same demonstrated path.

supplementary.note: 2015 original prFMN-dependent decarboxylation and cycloaddition proposal.

evidence.retrieved_excerpt: the methyl addition onto the double bond and the deprotonation step, are rate determining
evidence.limits: Primary isotope exchange and kinetic-isotope effects reject previous solvent-exchange report; both chemical steps contribute to rate. No free carbene or universal concerted closure claim.

supplementary.note: Primary mutational/chemical rescue supports catalytic bicarbonate, without directly visualizing every proton-transfer event.

evidence.retrieved_excerpt: cycling between mono-oxo-Mo(VI) and des-oxo-Mo(IV) forms via a DMSO-bound Mo(IV) intermediate
evidence.limits: Primary resonance Raman supports substrate oxygen-atom transfer and persistent dithiolene ligands; publisher open returned403, so indexed excerpt remains scope. Different from Mo-OH carbon attack/hydride-to-sulfido hydroxylation.

supplementary.note: Primary spectroscopic/electronic-structure study of DMSO reductase catalytic intermediate.

evidence.retrieved_excerpt: utilization of the enzyme-bound NADH for reduction of the eIF5A-imine intermediate
evidence.limits: Opened primary author abstract: substrate dehydrogenation generates bound NADH, acceptor addition consumes its fluorescence. Supporting isotope-trapping study locates enzyme imine and demonstrates transfer to acceptor.

supplementary.note: 1997 primary reductive trapping identifies Lys329 enzyme intermediate and labeled aminobutyl transfer to eIF5A. No split by homospermidine versus protein acceptor.

evidence.retrieved_excerpt: simultaneously bound to two lysine residues and partially vacating the active site
evidence.limits: Opened author abstract and correction notice. Covalent relay coordinates a path over20A and makes space for a second substrate. 2017 correction adds missing prior I320 structure citation; no withdrawal or changed result.

supplementary.note: Indexed primary body discusses five trapped covalent intermediates, substrate and product sites.

evidence.retrieved_excerpt: an iron-dependent sulphide transfer reaction from a conserved cysteine residue of the protein
evidence.limits: PubMed direct open CAPTCHA; indexed abstract and primary PMC figure2 text support protein-Cys sulfur source, DHA formation and single turnover. Do not generalize to catalytic THI4 homologs using external sulfide.

supplementary.note: Primary electron density supports loss of sulfur from the active-site cysteine to form dehydroalanine.

evidence.retrieved_excerpt: two lysine-asparagine isopeptide bonds generated by an intramolecular reaction
evidence.limits: Opened 2007 structural abstract establishes bonds; detailed proton relay is a primary QM/MM proposal. Card is generic fold-supported bond chemistry, with no pathogen engineering or potency claim.

supplementary.note: Primary 2011 JACS10.1021/ja107513t QM/MM: Lys attack, acidic residue proton relay, ammonia release.

evidence.retrieved_excerpt: MoaA accelerates the radical-mediated C-C bond formation
evidence.limits: Primary kinetic/EPR/shunt analysis of sugar-radical cyclization. Computed6-9-order acceleration is not made a universal card claim. Aminyl reduction is supported separately; MoaA does not perform downstream MoaC rearrangement.

supplementary.note: Primary 2021 aminyl radical reduction study supports auxiliary cluster electron donation and Arg proton donation via PCET; do not use obsolete oxidative termination hypothesis.

evidence.retrieved_excerpt: transient covalent linkage between the ε-amino group of K131 and the substrate’s C8 atom
evidence.limits: PMC direct open CAPTCHA, body retrieved through search. Four kinetically relevant intermediates and analog crystal support guided C8 insertion; exact complete elementary sequence remains a proposed model.

supplementary.note: Opened author's official institution copy of primary abstract verifies PNAS123(32)e2618523123,11Aug2026,DOI10.1073/pnas.2618523123. Published before current27Sep2026; not a preprint.

evidence.retrieved_excerpt: 2 molecules of thiocarboxylated MoaD per conversion of a single precursor Z molecule
evidence.limits: Primary stoichiometry and protein-associated monosulfurated intermediate support sequential sulfur-atom delivery. Detailed covalent thioester pathway is mechanistic proposal, not directly trapped atomic structure in this paper. Shared upstream E1 activation is not counted separately.

supplementary.note: Primary MoeB-MoaD apo/ATP/adenylate structures support carrier activation followed by thiocarboxylate formation; only downstream sulfur transfer defines this card.

evidence.retrieved_excerpt: carbon-centered radical produced by YydG, after Cα H-atom abstraction
evidence.limits: Opened primary body Results critical-H-donor section and Figure5 discussion: solvent-isotope incorporation and loss of epimerization/fragmentation in cysteine mutant support H-atom return. Auxiliary-cluster details of donor regeneration are tentative; no peptide sequence or antimicrobial engineering retained.

evidence.retrieved_excerpt: attack of the resultant backbone oxyanion onto the γ-phosphate of ATP
evidence.limits: Primary peptide-bound crystal, mutants and alternative-substrate cyclodehydration support shared YcaO amide activation. Hemiorthoamide/phosphorylated states are presumptive; do not claim direct intermediate crystal. Azoline, thioamide and amidine are grouped as one mechanism.

supplementary.note: Primary2018 enzymatic reconstitution: ATP/sulfide dependence and isotope/product analysis support backbone phosphorylation.

exclusions.reason: Existing selectivity card already names multiple-ion occupancy. Direct water-free versus water-mediated knock-on is contested and this source chiefly recasts same selectivity output; held rather than count.

Potentially distinct active transverse-gradient repetition, but retrieved standard explanations were reviews and modern model disagreement needs primary qualification. Not enough verified primary scope this batch.
Discrete nodal geometry and insulating myelin mainly modify existing regenerative electrical propagation; source also lacked readable abstract.
Premethylation of sulfur plus already-covered auxiliary-cluster sulfur donation lacks enough independent route beyond sequential combination; do not split substrate atoms or enzymes.
Replacement of sulfur nucleophile with selenium and tRNA attachment does not create another elimination-addition mechanism.
Useful repair chemistry but current radical-scission parent and radical-initiation cards cover core H-abstraction/beta-scission; biological lesion output alone is not enough.
Pentacyclic intermediate established, but detailed hydride-transfer/cycloaddition sequence has competing mechanistic proposals; held pending independent route beyond existing cycloaddition.

Organic cofactor self-oxygenation may have a distinct ring-contraction route, but cofactors differ and detailed atomic mechanism needs more direct evidence before separating from cofactor self-destruction.
The primary lysozyme example would provide more mechanism for the same current input/transformation/conditions, not a new independent effect.

exclusions.candidate: YcaO azoline versus thioamide versus amidine variants
exclusions.reason: Explicitly one card: shared amide nucleophilic addition, oxygen phosphorylation and elimination; nucleophile/output variants are not split.
